title: Corrections

sections.body: If something on this site is wrong, write to theworldofai@inkboxmail.com with the subject line Correction, or use the contact page. Include the address of the page and what is wrong, and a source for the right fact if you have one. Anyone can report an error, and reporting one is free. Corrections are the highest-priority mail this publication gets.

We answer within one business day. A confirmed error is fixed at the source, in the record the page is built from, and the fix publishes on the next daily run, usually within twenty-four hours. We do not defer a known error to a later review.

A confirmed error in a fact, a date, a case status or a citation is corrected on the page itself, and the page's verified date is updated. A corrected news story carries a dated correction note that says what was changed. Where an error on any other page was material, the correction is noted on that page as well. We do not silently rewrite.
A story or page that is withdrawn is not deleted. It is retained with a note saying why, and redirected where a replacement exists. Records, once published, are kept.
No payment or commercial relationship changes whether an error is corrected or how. The full rules for sourcing, automation and funding are in the editorial policy.

description: How to report an error on The World of AI, how quickly it is fixed, and how a correction is shown on the page.
